questions.label: Practice · A 78-year-old woman living alone in a two-story home has fallen three times in two weeks. She says she simply tripped. MMSE is 28/30, gait speed 0.7 m/s, tandem walking is impaired, and Romberg testing is positive. Vision is 20/40 in both eyes with cataracts. She takes hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg. Vitamin B12 is 180 pg/mL (laboratory lower limit 200); folate and TSH are normal. Which approach addresses the range of risk factors through a multifactorial falls-prevention plan?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with advanced chronic kidney disease, coronary artery disease, and recently diagnosed colon cancer has severe constipation and cramping abdominal pain after chemotherapy. He takes ondansetron, aspirin, atorvastatin, and metoprolol. Vital signs are stable; the abdomen is distended with hyperactive bowel sounds, and abdominal imaging shows fecal loading without obstruction. Which laxative does Hazzard advise against because of its greater adverse-effect risk in older adults?

Practice · An 84-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment (MMSE 24) and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m²) is hospitalized with pneumonia. On day three she develops acute confusion, visual hallucinations, and agitation; the CAM is positive. She pulls at an indwelling urinary catheter that is no longer medically needed. She is receiving levofloxacin, acetaminophen, amlodipine, and atorvastatin. Which initial intervention best follows Hazzard’s nonpharmacologic approach?

Practice · A 79-year-old man with diabetes and mild cognitive impairment has lost about 7 kg in four months. He takes small bites, chews extensively, reports food going 'the wrong way,' and has a wet, gurgly voice after meals. Medications are metformin 500 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily; creatinine clearance is 44 mL/min. Modified barium swallow shows vallecular residue and delayed swallow initiation. Which statement correctly characterizes rehabilitative swallowing therapy considered after this assessment?

Practice · A 75-year-old man with recently diagnosed subclinical hypothyroidism (initial TSH 8.2) returns after eight weeks of levothyroxine 25 micrograms daily. He feels more energetic and again walks his dog daily, but his wife reports new evening confusion. TSH is 2.8, free T4 is 1.3 ng/dL, and temperature is 36.8 degrees C. His medications include levothyroxine, atorvastatin 40 mg, and diphenhydramine 50 mg nightly for sleep. Which statement about diphenhydramine supports reviewing its use in this patient?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension and mild cognitive impairment (MMSE 22) presents after 3 days of productive cough, fever and delirium. He has fallen twice that day and missed medications. His usual drugs are metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Temperature is 38.8°C, BP 95/60 mmHg, pulse 110/min, respiratory rate 28/min and oxygen saturation 88% on room air. Chest radiography shows right lower-lobe consolidation; WBC is 16.2, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL (baseline 1.2) and glucose 340 mg/dL. Oxygenation and hemodynamic support are being addressed. Which infection-directed strategy accords with Hazzard while microbiology results are pending?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, stage 3 CKD (eGFR 45), and recent functional decline is scheduled for MitraClip placement. She now uses a walker and her daughter manages her medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg daily, and atorvastatin. She is anxious about general anesthesia. Which procedural plan is described in Hazzard?

Practice · A 72-year-old man reports worsening urinary frequency, nocturia four to five times nightly, and a weak stream for six months. His AUASI is 18. He has hypertension, diabetes, and recent falls, takes metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin, and lives alone. Which drug treats BPH-related lower urinary tract symptoms through selective alpha-1A blockade?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and moderate Alzheimer dementia lives with her daughter, who has discovered medication errors. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, donepezil 10 mg daily, and aspirin 81 mg daily. HbA1c is 7.2%, blood pressure is 145/85, and eGFR is 48. Which statement correctly identifies the source-described hypoglycemia concern in her oral diabetes regimen?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman is brought by her daughter for routine follow-up. She has fallen twice in the past month and seems more forgetful. She lives alone and manages her finances, but recently burned a pot while cooking. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily, amitriptyline 50 mg at night for neuropathic pain, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Blood pressure is 128/78 sitting and 108/65 after three minutes standing. Her Mini-Cog score is 2/5. Which approach to amitriptyline addresses the medication concern identified in Beers 2023?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman reports dizziness when wearing high-necked sweaters or adjusting necklaces. Yesterday she briefly lost consciousness during hair washing at a salon. She has coronary artery disease treated with stenting and hypertension, and takes aspirin 81 mg daily, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. If contraindications are excluded, which test directly evaluates suspected carotid sinus hypersensitivity?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with stable coronary disease, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) had his last myocardial infarction three years ago. He takes aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg, and metformin 1000 mg twice daily. LDL is 72 mg/dL and HbA1c 7.8%. His wife reports missed evening doses. Which prescribing approach directly addresses the regimen-complexity problem described by Hazzard?

Practice · An 80-year-old man has frailty with unintentional 15-lb weight loss, exhaustion, weakness, and slow walking speed, and stage 3b CKD (eGFR 36). He takes 12 medications, including atorvastatin 80 mg, aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol 100 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 40 mg. Blood pressure is 108/64 and albumin 3.1. Which approach follows Hazzard's principles for reviewing this medication burden?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with diabetes, coronary artery disease, and depression presents with dizziness and weakness. He takes metformin, atorvastatin, metoprolol 100 mg twice daily, lisinopril, paroxetine 40 mg daily, and recently added amitriptyline 75 mg for neuropathy. BP is 102/68 seated and 84/52 standing, heart rate is 58, and QTc is 492 ms. Which assessment of amitriptyline follows from the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

Practice · An 80-year-old man with a myocardial infarction 12 years ago, chronic stable angina, and stage 3a chronic kidney disease attends a medication review. He functions well and walks two miles daily without symptoms. He takes aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, amlodipine 5 mg, and atorvastatin 40 mg. Blood pressure is 128/76 mm Hg, heart rate is 64 beats/min, and a recent echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 55%. Before deciding whether to deprescribe metoprolol, which finding would support deprescribing under Hazzard's framework?

Practice · An 80-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and mild dementia has weight loss and frequent falls. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg, and aspirin 81 mg. BMI fell from 23 to 19 over 8 months; HbA1c is 6.4% and LDL is 68. She forgets meals and struggles with cooking. Grip strength is 14 kg, and she rises slowly while holding furniture. Which adjustment addresses the hypoglycemia risk emphasized by Hazzard?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension and mild cognitive impairment develops fatigue, difficulty shopping and a postural blood-pressure fall after starting amitriptyline for neuropathic pain. She also takes metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, amlodipine, atorvastatin and aspirin. Which change best addresses the new symptoms?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman attending a new-patient visit reports occasional urinary leakage but is embarrassed to discuss it. Her daughter reports daily laundry and a urine odor in the apartment. She takes hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, and diphenhydramine 50 mg nightly for sleep. Examination is normal apart from mild vulvar redness, and postvoid residual is 85 mL. During medication review, which approach to diphenhydramine is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Alzheimer disease (MMSE 18) is brought to the emergency department after two days of unusual behavior. His daughter recalls an unnamed constipation medicine. He is confused and has asterixis. Results are sodium 138, potassium 4.1, creatinine 1.4, and magnesium 4.8 mEq/L (laboratory reference range 1.5–2.5). His other medications are donepezil, memantine, and atorvastatin. Which statement about laxative safety supports investigating magnesium hydroxide exposure?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman has peripheral arterial disease (ABI 0.45), stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22), and a recent fall with hip fracture. Claudication now limits walking to 50 feet, and duplex shows 80% superficial femoral artery stenosis. She takes clopidogrel 75 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, and metoprolol 25 mg twice daily. When planning exercise within her safe capabilities, which walking approach is described for claudication?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman has recurrent near-syncope when rising from a chair after recently starting doxazosin 4 mg nightly for hypertension. Blood pressure is 158/78 supine and 122/68 after three minutes standing, with pulse rising from 68 to 74. Her daughter reports two falls this month and refusal to shower alone. She also takes hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg. Which medication-review approach follows the Beers recommendation for doxazosin used as an antihypertensive?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with diabetes and stage 3a chronic kidney disease is hospitalized for pneumonia. On the third day he develops new confusion, difficulty following commands and picking at the sheets; his wife reports that he was cognitively clear the day before. Medications include metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, ceftriaxone and as-needed diphenhydramine for sleep. Which approach fits the medication component of delirium management?
